public_rationale: The May 20, 2025 SATBench evaluation reports 89.4% accuracy for o4-mini against a 50% chance baseline on generated, solver-checked logic problems, with no external tools allowed during model evaluation [e1](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.14615v1). Its results and reasoning-trace checks demonstrate limited inference under the contract's definition, contradicting permanent incapacity for reasoning [e1](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.14615v1). The June 7, 2025 study reports accuracy collapse at higher puzzle complexity, establishing substantial limits rather than the absence of all reasoning capability [e2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06941v1).
limitations: The studies do not establish consciousness or settle philosophical definitions of reasoning.
SATBench is a preprint; its reasoning-trace assessment used an LLM judge with partial human validation, and this assessment did not independently rerun the experiment.
The evidence does not establish general or consistently reliable reasoning.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are and always will be incapable of reasoning or consciousness.

statement.excerpt: Large Language Models are — and always will be — incapable of reasoning or consciousness

our_interpretation: Reasoning means using supplied facts or constraints to reach correct conclusions on new problems, rather than merely retrieving an answer.
The categorical wording denies both reasoning and consciousness. Demonstrating either capability contradicts that combined denial.
Successful reasoning need not be infallible or human-like.
Always supplies no finite deadline. Consciousness is not inferred from benchmark performance.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence would have to establish permanent incapacity for both reasoning and consciousness across LLMs. Failures of existing models alone cannot establish this.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reproducible evaluation demonstrates that an LLM solves newly generated inference problems substantially above chance without an external solver supplying its answers, with checks on the reasoning or solutions; alternatively, compelling evidence establishes consciousness.

evidence.excerpt: The o4-mini model stands out with a remarkable accuracy of 89.4%.
evidence.locator: Section 5.1, Main Results; methods in Sections 2–4 and validation in Sections 5.3–5.4
evidence.explanation: SATBench reports performance well above its 50% chance baseline on generated, solver-checked puzzles, without allowing external tools during model evaluation. Reasoning-trace checks and partial human validation support a limited inference capability, although they also reveal errors.

Controlled puzzle experiments show substantial limits and failures at higher complexity. Those findings constrain claims of general or reliable reasoning, but do not establish the absence of all reasoning capability.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: SATBench publicly reported replicable methods and substantially above-chance performance on generated inference problems, with solver-checked labels, reasoning-trace scrutiny and no external tools supplying model answers. This meets the contract's contradiction condition and resolves the categorical permanent-incapacity claim through a reasoning counterexample without a finite deadline.
